To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inhibition of glutamate uptake by the glutamate transport inhibitors, THA and PCD, results in the degeneration of motor neurons in the rat's spinal cord organotypic cultures.

chronic glutamate uptake inhibition by threohydroxyl-aspartate (THAs) and L-trans-Pyrrolidine- 2,4-diacarboxylate(PDC) results in the slow degeneration of rat's motor neurons (MNs) and distinct glial changes involving astrocytes.
chronic excitotoxicity in a rat model of amyotrophic lateral slerosis in vitro is associated with the degeneration of motor neurons and the development of astroglial abnormalities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of astrocyte in neurodegenerative processes and with the possibility of astrocyte involvement in the development of ALS.
the role of astroglial cells in the pathogenesis of ALS and other neurodegenerative disorders.
the study of the mechanisms of neurodegeneration induced by chronic glutamate excitotoxic insults in a model of ALS in vitro and with the role of glial cells in the pathogenesis of the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the astrocytes in the ALS model of slow glutamatergic excitotoxicity undergo a number of changes that include vacuolation, proliferation and accumulation of smooth endoplamic reticulum.
astrocytes may be actively involved in the pathogenesis of ALS and other neurodegenerative disorders associated with chronic glutamate excitotoxic injury.

glia and neurons are both affected by glutamate excitotoxic mechanisms and that glia and their dysfunction are not only a consequence of neuronal degeneration, but also a contributing factor to the neurodegeneration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the slow glutamate excitotoxicty in vitro model mimicks some of the pathogenic features of the human ALS disease and may be used to study the mechanisms of the disease.
astrocytes play an active role in the induction and propagation in the degeneration of MNs in an ALS model.
the astroglial changes in this model are consistent with the hypothesis of a chronic excitotoxic process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
astrocytes are not only passive bystanders but also actively involved in the process of neuronal death in ALS.
astrocytes play a significant role in the pathogenesis of ALS.
astroglial alterations are a common feature of neurodegenerative disorders.
